steps: Hold your dominant hand up in front of your body at chest height.
Sweep the hand backward in an arc that travels over your dominant shoulder.
Let the hand pass well behind the shoulder so the backward path reads as time gone by.
Keep your palm facing your body through the whole arc.
Use a bigger, more emphatic sweep when you mean a longer time ago — size shows distance.
Pair it with a time word first, like THREE YEAR, so the listener knows how far back.
tip: AGO borrows the PAST sign: one backward sweep over the shoulder, bigger for 'long ago'.

steps: Hold your dominant hand beside your head in a bent-hand shape, fingers together and curved.
Start with the hand near the side of your head, roughly at ear or temple height.
Shoot the hand upward quickly, letting it drift slightly forward as it rises.
Keep the movement short and brisk — it shows a person growing taller.
End with the hand clearly above its starting height, fingers still bent.
Stay neutral-faced; this sign also means TALL, so context picks the meaning.
tip: A bent hand springing up beside the head — picture someone growing up taller.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an R, crossing the middle finger over the index finger.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up or toward you.
Touch the palm side of the R hand down onto the flat palm.
Lift the R hand off an inch or two, shift it downward a couple of inches, and touch down again.
Make the two contacts firm and crisp — the double tap reads as an official rule.
Keep both hands in your chest-level signing space with a matter-of-fact expression.
tip: RULE is LAW initialized: tap an R hand twice on a flat palm.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you with the palm facing up.
Point your dominant index finger straight down toward that open palm.
Jab the fingertip down onto the palm twice in quick, firm taps.
Keep the jabs short and pointed, like marking an amount due on a bill.
Use a single jab for the verb 'owe' and the double jab for the noun 'bill'.
Keep a neutral expression; the taps carry the meaning, not the face.
tip: Double-jab your open palm with an index finger — like pointing out the total on an invoice.

steps: Raise both hands in front of you in V handshapes, index and middle fingers extended.
Hold your non-dominant V hand steady with the fingers pointing up and the palm facing back.
Rest the fingertips of your dominant V lightly on top of the non-dominant fingertips.
Flutter the dominant index and middle fingers up and down in alternation, like a see-saw.
Keep the base hand still while only the top fingers rock back and forth.
Pair it with raised eyebrows when you ask a choice question, such as TEA EITHER COFFEE?
tip: Two V hands rocking fingertip to fingertip — picture weighing two choices against each other.

steps: Hold up your non-dominant hand in a five handshape, palm facing toward your dominant side and fingers pointing up.
Flatten your dominant hand into a B shape, fingers together and thumb tucked in.
Slide the pinkie-side edge of the flat hand down between the middle and ring fingers of the raised hand.
Move it as if slipping a document into a file folder.
Do the insertion once for the verb 'to file', twice for the noun 'a file or document'.
Keep the raised hand steady and upright while the flat hand does the work.
tip: Slipping the flat hand between the upright fingers is filing a document into a folder — twice for the noun.

steps: Raise both hands up high near head height, off to your dominant side.
Start with the hands in the loose open shape used for QUOTE or TITLE.
Sweep both hands downward toward the front of your torso.
As the hands drop, bend the index and middle fingers into bent-V shapes.
Land the movement in front of your chest or stomach, showing data coming down to you.
Keep the path smooth and vertical — the downward travel is what says 'download'.
tip: Hands start high and rain down into bent Vs at your torso — files coming down to your device.

steps: Hold both hands up in front of your chest in open five handshapes, fingers spread.
Start with the palms facing you and the fingertips pointing upward.
Twist both wrists sharply so the palms snap to face outward, away from you.
Make the twist quick and decisive — one firm twist says the matter is FINAL.
Keep the elbows relaxed and the hands close together in your central signing space.
Match a firm, settled expression to the finality of the statement.
tip: One sharp twist of both open hands from palm-in to palm-out — a single twist reads as 'final'.
